title: AWS Bedrock AgentCore Web Search gains domain and date filters, expands to EU and APAC
subtitle: The managed web-retrieval tool for AI agents now lets each request narrow sources and time windows, and is live in Ireland and Tokyo alongside N. Virginia.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: AWS shipped an update to Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore on August 20 that adds two per-request controls agents did not have before: an allow-and-block list of domains, and inclusive from-and-to date bounds on published sources. The service — a managed connector that lets an agent call out to the live web without data leaving the customer's AWS environment — was originally scoped to us-east-1 (N. Virginia). This update makes it available in eu-west-1 (Ireland) and ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo), which brings it inside Europe's and Japan's data-residency perimeters for regulated workloads.

The filters matter because production agents were already using Web Search as their grounding layer for real answers, and the failure modes were predictable — a customer-support agent citing a competitor's press release, or a research agent quoting a 2019 blog post as if it were current. Runtime domain filtering means the agent can restrict itself to trusted publications on one call and open the web on the next, without an admin round-trip. Date filtering lets an agent answer 'what changed this week' without swimming through older results that dominate rankings.

The bigger story is where the middleware for agents is congealing. AWS is now positioning AgentCore as the runtime — Web Search, Gateway, Memory, Runtime — while the protocol layer is consolidating under the Linux Foundation-directed Agentic AI Foundation, which absorbed Google's A2A protocol on the same day this update shipped. That leaves the model layer (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Alibaba, Zhipu) increasingly interchangeable and the infrastructure layer (AgentCore, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure AI Foundry) as the durable moat, at least for enterprise buyers who care about data residency and audit trails.

A note for learners: when an agent 'searches the web,' you are picking a search operator with opinions — a set of domains, a ranking function, a freshness policy, a citation format. The new AgentCore filters make those choices explicit on every call. For anyone building agents against a specific corpus (regulatory, medical, financial), configuring the domain allowlist and date range is now a first-class part of the prompt, not a wish.
